_comment: PLAT-35 — TIER 2. THE PERCEPTUAL THRESHOLDS, ONE PER NAMED VIEW.
Cross-Renderer-Visual-Alignment.md §2: tier 2 covers what structure cannot
express — rendered colour, weight, spacing, density — and its thresholds
between two renderers are necessarily looser than between two commits of
one. The methodology's ratchet rule carries across UNCHANGED:
**A THRESHOLD RAISED TWICE IS A DEFECT IN THE CAPTURE, NOT IN THE
THRESHOLD.** Ratcheting a limit to keep a gate green converts the gate
into decoration; the second raise triggers an investigation of what is
non-deterministic instead.
That rule is enforced rather than quoted: every threshold carries its own
`history`, and `test_cross_renderer_visual_alignment.nim` fails when any
entry's history holds two increases. A rule with no reader is a sentence.
THRESHOLDS ARE PER VIEW AND NOT GLOBAL. A dense table tolerates far less
drift than a mostly-empty shell, and one global number is either too loose
for the former or permanently red on the latter.
WHAT TIER 2 CAN AND CANNOT DO TODAY, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN IMPLIED BY A
GREEN RUN.
The Electron side captures pixels: `visual-alignment-capture.spec.ts` writes
a PNG per named view under `src/tests/visual/captures/electron/`, and its
tier-1 canary asserts two captures of one settled frame are byte-identical.
The GPUI side captures NO PIXELS. isonim-gpui's Rust shim is built in this
workspace WITHOUT `--features gpui-backend`, so `createWindow` opens nothing
— `src/frontend/gpui/main.nim`'s own header says so, and
`src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_gpui_editing_surface.nim` records that this
host has no display server for it either. So the CROSS-RENDERER arm of tier
2 is BLOCKED on `PLAT35-VG1`, and the thresholds below are declared, gated
for integrity, and not yet applied to a GPUI image.
They are declared NOW rather than when the blocker clears, for one reason
that is not tidiness: a threshold chosen after seeing the first diff is a
threshold chosen to make that diff pass. These were chosen from what the two
rasterisers are known to differ by — text shaping and subpixel policy on
dense text, blending on tinted overlays — before either image existed.
`maxDifferingPixelRatio` is the fraction of pixels allowed to differ
perceptually, in per-mille, against the paired capture of the SAME scenario
in the other front-end.

shell.why: Mostly flat surfaces and a toolbar; the text that is present is short. The loosest number in the set would be wrong here.

editor.why: Dense monospaced text across three quarters of the window. Two text shapers disagree on nearly every glyph edge, and this is the view where that costs the most pixels.

state.why: Dense text plus inline value chips, whose tinted backgrounds are blended differently by the two renderers.

calltrace.why: A list: fewer glyphs than the editor, more than the shell.

eventLog.why: A data table. Column rules are one-pixel features and are exactly what a subpixel policy moves.

editorWithMark.why: The editor's density plus a gutter glyph and a line highlight, which is the one place in the set where a tinted overlay sits under text. The loosest number in the set, and it is the loosest for a named reason rather than by default.
